questions.question: Sana wants to find out what games her Ayeeyo played long ago. What is the best way to find out?
questions.options: Ask Ayeeyo and listen carefully to her answer | Ask her baby sister instead | Guess and tell everyone her guess | Say nothing and hope to find out one day
questions.correctAnswer: Ask Ayeeyo and listen carefully to her answer
questions.explanation: Ayeeyo was there long ago, so she really knows. Asking a person and listening carefully is a lovely way to find things out.

questions.question: Leila wants to find out what a market seller does at work. Which question should she ask?
questions.options: Do you like my new shoes? | What is your favourite colour? | How old is your cat? | What do you do in your job?
questions.correctAnswer: What do you do in your job?
questions.explanation: Leila wants to learn about the job, so she should ask a question about the job. The other questions are friendly, but they will not tell her about the work.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: What do we know about jobs?

questions.question: Sami wants to find out what a doctor does all day. Who is the best person to ask?
questions.options: His teddy bear | A doctor | Nobody at all | A baby
questions.correctAnswer: A doctor
questions.explanation: A doctor knows their own job best. When we want to find something out, we ask someone who really knows.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: What do we know about jobs?

questions.question: Karim wants to find out what a little plant needs to grow. What is a good way to find out?
questions.options: Ask his friend what is for lunch | Look closely at a real plant and ask a grown-up about it | Put the plant in a dark cupboard and forget it | Close his eyes and think about football
questions.correctAnswer: Look closely at a real plant and ask a grown-up about it
questions.explanation: Looking closely and asking questions are how we find things out. A real plant and a helpful grown-up can teach Karim a lot.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: What kind of garden would be best?

questions.question: Zane wants to find out all the ways his family uses water at home. What should he do?
questions.options: Stay in one room and guess | Tick every box without looking | Walk around his home with a grown-up and look, then tick each way he finds | Ask the cat
questions.correctAnswer: Walk around his home with a grown-up and look, then tick each way he finds
questions.explanation: Looking with his own eyes and ticking what he finds means Zane's answers are real, not guesses. That is what finding out means.

questions.question: Sana asks her Awoowe one question, and he starts telling a long story about when he was little. What should Sana do to find out the most?
questions.options: Cover her ears | Start talking about her own day | Listen carefully all the way to the end | Walk away in the middle
questions.correctAnswer: Listen carefully all the way to the end
questions.explanation: Stories from older people are full of things to find out. Listening all the way to the end helps Sana learn the most.

questions.question: Karim asks everyone in his family which garden they like best. He makes a mark on his paper for each answer. Why are the marks helpful?
questions.options: They make the paper heavier | They stop the family from talking | They water the garden | They help him remember and count all the answers
questions.correctAnswer: They help him remember and count all the answers
questions.explanation: When we find out lots of answers, marks on paper keep them safe. Later we can count the marks and see what we found.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: What kind of garden would be best?

questions.question: Amal says the tap in the yard drips all day. Zane is not sure. What should Zane do before he tells anyone else?
questions.options: Tell everyone it never drips | Say it drips without looking | Go with a grown-up and look at the tap himself | Forget all about it
questions.correctAnswer: Go with a grown-up and look at the tap himself
questions.explanation: Good finder-outers check with their own eyes. Looking at the tap tells Zane if it really drips.

questions.question: Sana wants to find out how children help at home. She can ask one friend, or she can ask all five of her friends. Why is asking all five better?
questions.options: It is faster | Her friends will do her jobs for her | She will hear many different answers | One friend always knows everything
questions.correctAnswer: She will hear many different answers
questions.explanation: Every family is different, so every friend may say something new. More answers help Sana find out much more.

questions.question: Karim says: 'I like the flower garden best, because the flowers bring bees and butterflies.' What did Karim do well?
questions.options: He said every garden is bad | He copied his friend's answer | He kept his idea a secret | He said which garden he liked and gave his reason why
questions.correctAnswer: He said which garden he liked and gave his reason why
questions.explanation: Saying what you like and then saying why is a big Stage 1 skill. Karim's 'because' tells everyone his reason.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: What kind of garden would be best?

questions.question: Leila says: 'I would like to be a doctor.' Which of these gives a reason for her choice?
questions.options: My shoes are red | A doctor is a word | I said it first | Because I want to help people get better
questions.correctAnswer: Because I want to help people get better
questions.explanation: A reason tells us why. 'Because I want to help people get better' explains why Leila chose that job.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: What do we know about jobs?

questions.question: Karim is sorting plants into two groups: 'we can eat it' and 'just lovely to look at'. Where does the tomato go?
questions.options: Outside all the groups | In the 'we can eat it' group | In the 'just lovely to look at' group | In the toys group
questions.correctAnswer: In the 'we can eat it' group
questions.explanation: We eat tomatoes, so the tomato belongs in the eating group. Sorting things into groups helps us think about what we found.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: What kind of garden would be best?

questions.question: Zane brushes his teeth and leaves the tap running the whole time. What happens because of this?
questions.options: Nothing happens at all | The water is saved for later | More water appears in the sea | Clean water is wasted down the drain
questions.correctAnswer: Clean water is wasted down the drain
questions.explanation: A running tap keeps pouring water that nobody is using. Thinking about what happens because of what we do helps us make kind choices.

questions.question: The tap at school drips all day long. Which action would help solve the problem?
questions.options: Tell a grown-up about the dripping tap | Sing a song to the tap | Watch the drips and do nothing | Leave the tap dripping
questions.correctAnswer: Tell a grown-up about the dripping tap
questions.explanation: Telling a grown-up means the tap can be mended, so no more water is wasted. Choosing an action that helps is how we solve problems.

questions.question: Karim's chart shows the marks his family made: the food garden got 2 marks, the flower garden got 5 marks, and the little pots got 1 mark. What does his chart tell him?
questions.options: The little pots were the most popular | Everyone chose the food garden | The flower garden was the most popular | The chart cannot tell him anything
questions.correctAnswer: The flower garden was the most popular
questions.explanation: 5 marks is more than 2 and more than 1, so most people chose the flower garden. Counting the marks tells Karim what he found out.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: What kind of garden would be best?

questions.question: Sana has finished her My Family poster. Her grown-up asks her to look back and think. Which sentence shows Sana thinking about her learning?
questions.options: My crayon is green | I want to go outside now | The thing I liked best was drawing my Ayeeyo | Posters are made of paper
questions.correctAnswer: The thing I liked best was drawing my Ayeeyo
questions.explanation: Looking back means saying what you liked and what you found out. 'The thing I liked best was ...' is a looking-back sentence.

questions.question: After the water project, Zane's grown-up asks: 'What is one new thing you found out?' Which answer shows Zane looking back at what he learned?
questions.options: I found out that a dripping tap wastes good water | I like football | Can we play now? | I am six years old
questions.correctAnswer: I found out that a dripping tap wastes good water
questions.explanation: 'I found out ...' shows Zane is looking back at his learning. The other answers do not tell us what he learned.

questions.question: Sana is showing her My Family poster to her class. What should she do?
questions.options: Roll the poster up quickly | Point to each person and say who they are | Hide the poster behind her back | Look at the floor and say nothing
questions.correctAnswer: Point to each person and say who they are
questions.explanation: Show and tell means showing your work and telling people about it. Pointing and naming each person shares Sana's poster clearly.

questions.question: While Sana talks about her poster, her friend Amal wants to be a good listener. What should Amal do?
questions.options: Talk loudly about her own poster at the same time | Shut her eyes and hum | Look at Sana, listen, and then ask a friendly question | Walk away while Sana is talking
questions.correctAnswer: Look at Sana, listen, and then ask a friendly question
questions.explanation: Good listeners look, listen, and ask a kind question at the end. That shows Sana her words matter.

questions.question: A grown-up asks Leila: 'What job would you like to do?' Which answer tells them the most?
questions.options: Yes | I would like to be a teacher, and I would use books and a board | I forget | A job is a job
questions.correctAnswer: I would like to be a teacher, and I would use books and a board
questions.explanation: The long answer says the job and the tools, so it really answers the question. When we answer, we try to share helpful details.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: What do we know about jobs?

questions.question: Zane wants his family to know his idea for saving water. What is the clearest way to share it?
questions.options: Whisper it so quietly that nobody hears | Shout 'Water!' and run away | Say nothing and hope they guess | Say: 'I can save water by turning off the tap while I brush my teeth'
questions.correctAnswer: Say: 'I can save water by turning off the tap while I brush my teeth'
questions.explanation: A clear, full sentence tells everyone exactly what Zane's idea is. Sharing clearly helps other people understand and join in.

questions.question: Karim and Sami are planting seeds together, and there is only one watering can. What is the kind way to work together?
questions.options: Hide the can so nobody can water | Stop planting and go home | Take turns with the watering can | Grab the can and keep it
questions.correctAnswer: Take turns with the watering can
questions.explanation: Taking turns means everyone gets a go. That is how friends share and work well together.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: What kind of garden would be best?

questions.question: Leila and her friends are playing the acting game. Leila acts out a job and her friend guesses it. What is fair to do next?
questions.options: Let her friend have a turn at acting | Tell her friend the game is over for her | Stop the game so nobody has a turn | Leila acts every single time
questions.correctAnswer: Let her friend have a turn at acting
questions.explanation: In a fair game, everyone gets a turn. Giving her friend a go keeps the game happy for both of them.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: What do we know about jobs?

questions.question: Amal and Karim are making one garden poster together. Amal wants to draw flowers, and Karim wants to draw tomatoes. What is the best way to work together?
questions.options: Talk about both ideas and draw flowers and tomatoes together | Stop making the poster at all | Each one hides their crayons from the other | Karim decides alone and does not listen
questions.correctAnswer: Talk about both ideas and draw flowers and tomatoes together
questions.explanation: When friends work together, they listen to both ideas. A garden with flowers and tomatoes uses Amal's idea and Karim's idea.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: What kind of garden would be best?

questions.question: Zane tells his family: 'Every drop counts!' His little sister does not understand what he means. What should Zane do?
questions.options: Tell her she is too little to know | Say it faster and louder | Say it again slowly and show her at the tap | Give up and walk away
questions.correctAnswer: Say it again slowly and show her at the tap
questions.explanation: When someone does not understand, we can say it another way and show them. That is kind, clear sharing.
